title: Personality Changes
paragraphs: “So, Rorick-san. You said you had something to consult us about. What’s the matter?”
“Yes, about that…”

Here’s what this Rorick fellow had to say. Apparently, Rorick has a master he serves—or rather, a princess of low standing whom he is tasked with protecting. She has almost no claim to the throne, and one of her parents is said to be a wealthy noblewoman. In short, she has a sharp tongue, can’t be honest, and tends to be misunderstood. But when she sees someone in trouble, she helps them from the shadows. Despite her difficult personality, she’s a truly kind person at heart. Rorick and two others became knights alongside him, and they all grew up together as childhood friends. They were all people who deeply understood her.
“Haa…”
“Is there really a need for a personal history lesson?”
“Well, I thought you needed to know the context before I proceeded…”
“So, what happened?”
“It was about four months ago…”
While enjoying horseback riding, the young lady suddenly fell off her horse. Whether it was due to dizziness or simply losing her balance, Rorick couldn’t determine from his account.
“For about three days after that, she remained unconscious, hovering between life and death.”
“So, she woke up after three days?”
“Yes… but—”
Back to Rorick’s story. When she woke up, her manner of speaking had improved dramatically, and she had become honest and outgoing, like a completely different person.
“Her personality changed?”
“Yes, that’s correct. But… sometimes, the way she looks at us feels different… like she’s someone else.”
“Couldn’t it be something like multiple personalities?”
“Yeah. I’ve seen stories on TV about how a shock to the head can cause that…”
I’ve seen that too. Watching dramas was essential for keeping up conversations with the pigs. Because of that, I often watched TV at night.
“That’s not all. She’s been acting coquettish with men other than us, demanding gifts… and she’s also started distancing herself from women she used to be close with.”
“She’s completely become a different person, hasn’t she?”

“Yes. But her parents and everyone around her are very happy about the change. However, recently, she’s been saying she wants to try adventuring… and we, her childhood friends, know that she used to despise killing.”
“Could it be personality changes stemming from memory loss?”

“And… she acts like she knows things she’s never been told… but… she’s wrong. Like, about the friction between my parents or issues with my siblings. There are too many inconsistencies for it to just be memory confusion… and the other two knights feel the same sense of unease.”
Hmm… I don’t get it. Even Father groans in frustration.
“So, what’s the conclusion here?”
Ren, sounding irritated, pressed Rorick for an answer. This really is a confusing request.

“Recently, I’ve heard that the Four Cardinal Heroes have been capturing adventurers with unknown backgrounds and ambitious noble offspring. The reason is due to the disasters caused by the waves and…”
“I see. So, you came to ask if the person you’re protecting might fall into that category.”
“For now, we’re focusing on individuals who seem to have come from another world… but aren’t heroes, and noble offspring who have shown inexplicable talent since childhood.”
Oh! Finally, some work after a while!
“If they’re suspicious, extermination is the only option!”
“Please! I beg you, anything but that!”
Oh? Rorick is pleading with me. But I won’t stop.
“Motoyasu, calm down.”
“Naofumi-san, what should we do? This is a type of consultation we haven’t had before.”
“Hmm… I feel like I’ve heard a similar story somewhere before.”
“So do I.”
“Naofumi and Itsuki’s worlds seem to have a lot of those kinds of stories.”
“Ren, you’re too obsessed with VR games and PvP to know about this stuff. Motoyasu wouldn’t know either.”
“Indeed, that’s right!”
“Did something like that exist in my world too?”
Ren muttered to himself, feeling a sense of exclusion from the conversation. It’s fine. I don’t know about it either. For now, I’ll just give him a kind look as if we’re comrades.
Oh? My eyes met Ren’s. He quickly looked away.
What’s that supposed to mean?
“Ren, don’t you remember? The battle with the Ghost Princess of Melromarc.”
“Hm? That princess… she was an unforgettable enemy for many reasons, but…”
“Technically, it’s a little different, but think back to the state she was in before she manifested.”
“Right… she had possessed a royal woman with a claim to the throne… Wait, could it be!?”
It seems Father has realized what he was trying to explain to Ren.
“It’s just a possibility, but… there’s a pattern in stories where someone dies and ends up possessing a person from another world.”
In Father’s explanation, the host dies, and the invading soul enters the body, bringing it back to life. Apparently, there are other variations of this as well.
“I’ve encountered something similar. A suspected case of supernatural abilities.”
“There are so many types of interworld transfers…”
“Yes, we don’t know what our enemy’s goal is, but based on past trends, it’s entirely possible.”
“But if that’s the case…”
I raise my spear.
First, I’ll kill the host, and when the real entity comes out, I’ll blow it to pieces! Rorick clasps his hands together as if pleading.
“It might be easier than having their body controlled by someone else forever… but let’s look for another method. It’s not like our assumptions are necessarily correct.”
“Yes, but if our assumptions are right, how do we separate the entity that’s possessing them?”
“In these kinds of cases, it seems like anti-magic or religious rituals could work.”
“But there was that ghost that had taken over the church…”
Silence filled the room. The Filolials and the assistant, who couldn’t follow the complex conversation, tilted their heads.
Did the rival understand?
“What should we do…?”
“Why don’t we ask if the kingdom has a department that handles these kinds of matters?”
“Oh, that’s a good idea. Besides, we’re just speculating here. It could simply be delusions caused by memory confusion.”
“That’s true. Alright, we’ve received the request. We’ll take action later.”
“Rorick-san and the other two knights, please continue acting as usual. And make sure not to let this information slip out.”
After saying that, Rorick nodded with a look of relief, saluted, and left. What a troublesome case this is.
“So, what’s the plan now?”
“I’m thinking of consulting the clinic and the church to see if there’s any precedent. There might even be something about it in the legends of the heroes.”
“Haven’t they already tried that? Isn’t solving things through that kind of legend a standard approach?”
“Can you really go and say, ‘The princess we’re protecting might be possessed by someone else’ to them? From what I’ve seen, they want to keep this under wraps.”
“If something like a purification ritual at the church actually worked… it’d just feel like a bad joke.”

“I once heard from a pig who was knowledgeable about the occult. In other countries, they call evil spirits ‘demons’ and perform exorcisms. Of course, they also claim that children who say things they don’t like are possessed by demons and abuse them.”
“Motoyasu-kun… something’s off about that…”
Oh? Did I get something wrong?
“But is this really something for the heroes to deal with?”
Ren has a point.
What would I do? If one day, my body was taken over by someone who wasn’t me…
“Come to think of it, back then, Father was possessed by a cursed weapon and acted like a completely different person.”
“Ugh… we’re bringing that up again…?”
Father stammered and looked troubled. Don’t get me wrong, though. Even back then, Father was a good person. Though we ended up on opposite sides as a result.

“It’s not exactly a consultation, but since they’ve been gathering information on reincarnators and trippers, I think they’re bringing this case forward as an example. The people around them are getting suspicious too, after all.”
